newsitem.title: GERMANY: Varta to return to profit in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Varta to return to profit in 1997.

text.p: German battery maker Varta AG said on Thursday sales rose by one percent in 1996 to 1.99 billion marks ($1.2 billion) despite the disposal of its loss-making industrial batteries unit.
The company said losses after restructuring charges fell by three-quarters from the year before, which was below planned targets, but added it expected to return to profit this year.
On the 1997 outlook, the company said: "A satisfactory start to the new business year confirms our optimism."
Varta said it expected growth in the European market to remain weak this year and price competition fierce, but growth in other markets like Latin America would be strong.
A breakdown of 1996 turnover showed that German sales fell by eight percent, while foreign sales rose by three percent to take 67 percent of Varta's total sales.
Sales of batteries for cars and electrical appliances both rose by one percent, while the Varta-Plastic division expanded by 11 percent.
The company's workforce rose by 16 percent and investment increased by 14 percent to 124 million marks.
